verdict.rationale: Pylon documents that the support agent only handles issues it is assigned to, giving admins 'full control of which customer issues your AI agent interacts with'. That is a product-level way to keep certain issues away from the agent. But nothing documents marking topics such as legal threats, cancellations or security as human-only, auto-detecting those topics, or a hard guarantee that the agent hands off mid-conversation; natural-language runbooks are guidance, not an enforced block. Missing for 10: topic-based human-only/escalation rules, automatic topic detection that blocks the agent, enforced handoff guarantees, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a support ops lead, I mark topics as human-only — legal threats, cancellations, security — and the agent never freelances on them

citations.quote: This means you have full control of which customer issues your AI agent interacts with.
You can also assign an individual issue to your AI agent, the same way you might normally assign an issue to a team member.
Write instructions in natural language to help your AI Agent handle specific scenarios.
